entities.name: Majd ad-Dīn Ibn Athir
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Majd ad-Dīn Ibn Athir was a prominent hadith specialist, philologist, grammarian, lexicographer, biographer, litterateur, and a jurist of the Shafi'i school. Born in the 12th century, he is regarded as one of the leading hadith scholars of the seventh century A.H. Ibn Athir's works span multiple fields, including the collection and analysis of hadiths, which are crucial to understanding Islamic theology and jurisprudence. His magnum opus, the 'Alf Lila al-Ni'amah', is a comprehensive collection of 1,000 narratives that provide insights into the lives of prominent figures in Islamic history. Ibn Athir's influence can be seen in the work of later scholars, including the renowned hadith collector, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani. Through his writings, Ibn Athir has left a lasting legacy in the fields of Islamic scholarship and jurisprudence, contributing to a deeper understanding of Islamic theology and the lives of its most influential figures.

Ibn Athir's significance extends beyond his individual contributions to the broader context of Islamic scholarship during the medieval period. His works reflect the intellectual and cultural currents of his time, including the importance of hadith collection and analysis in Islamic theology. As a leading figure in the Shafi'i school, Ibn Athir's influence can be seen in the development of Islamic jurisprudence and the interpretation of Islamic texts. Despite the passage of centuries, Ibn Athir's works remain a vital source of information for scholars and researchers seeking to understand the history and development of Islamic thought.

entities.summary: Majd ad-Dīn Ibn Athir was a prominent hadith specialist, philologist, grammarian, lexicographer, biographer, litterateur, and a jurist of the Shafi'i school who lived in Cizre, Ladin, during the 12th century. Born in 1150, he is regarded as one of the leading hadith scholars of the seventh century A.H. Ibn Athir's scholarly works span multiple disciplines, including history, theology, and law. His biographical writings on prominent figures such as the Prophet Muhammad and the Umayyad caliphs have become foundational texts in Islamic scholarship. Ibn Athir's influence extends beyond the Islamic world, as his writings have been studied by scholars across various religious traditions. His contributions to the field of hadith scholarship have helped shape the understanding of the Prophet's teachings and the history of the Islamic world. The transmission of his works has continued through various manuscripts and printed editions, ensuring his intellectual legacy endures. Ibn Athir's emphasis on the importance of preserving and transmitting knowledge has inspired generations of scholars and historians. His work has been recognized as a vital component of Islamic intellectual history, providing valuable insights into the social, cultural, and religious contexts of the medieval Islamic world.
